scope: frontend alignment, frontend tests, UI/provider consistency reports

dimensions.name: test_alignment
dimensions.evidence: npm test passes 13 frontend test files, including module isolation, permission management, execution provider, and auth flow coverage.

dimensions.name: capability_driven_architecture_alignment
dimensions.evidence: Navigation and route expectations now assert product capability entries instead of legacy admin.modules/settings assumptions.

dimensions.name: product_navigation_consistency
dimensions.evidence: Visible sidebar product entries are Users, Organizations, Permissions, Logs, and Approvals.

dimensions.name: ui_backend_binding
dimensions.evidence: Users, Permissions assignments, Logs, and Approvals list are proxy-backed; Organizations remains UI-only.

dimensions.name: feature_completeness
dimensions.evidence: Users is functional, Permissions is embedded in Users, Logs and Approvals are read-only, and Organizations is an empty shell.

dimensions.name: action_layer_completeness
dimensions.evidence: Approvals approve/reject/request actions, organization lifecycle/member actions, logs filtering/export, and standalone permissions management are not exposed.

dimensions.name: verification_stability
dimensions.evidence: npm run typecheck, npm run verify, and npm test all pass from frontend package scripts.

aligned_product_navigation.label: Permissions
aligned_product_navigation.api_binding: Permission assignment APIs are bound inside Users; standalone page has no action layer

residual_risks: Organizations is visible as a product entry but has no frontend proxy/API binding.
Approvals list is bound, but approval request/approve/reject APIs are not exposed through the frontend proxy and no UI action layer exists.
Permissions has real assignment actions inside Users, while /permissions is an empty guidance page.
Hidden legacy/read-only pages still exist as direct routes and are reported rather than removed.
